messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 504 errors observed at apigw edge tier for multiple customer vhosts starting ~03:12Z. Currently 30% 504s for requests hitting origin-fanout. Alert: apigw.edge.5xx.rate > 20% for 5m. SLO impact: degraded. Paging @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: On it — taking lead. @eng-runtime please stand by. First triage: are we seeing origin timeouts, proxy queueing, or an upstream flapping?

raj: I see spike in origin latencies at 03:10Z on metric origin.request.lat p95 -> 6.2s. Correlates with increased inflight connections on edge pool A. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/apigw/spike (link)

emma: Confirmed from logs — nginx upstream timed out: 
```
[03:12:18] upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.5.2, server: vhost-payflow
```

alex: Recent config change? I deployed an edge-proxy template at 03:05Z with keepalive and aggressive connection reuse. Rolling back?

eng-runtime: We rolled edge-proxy 1.2.7 -> 1.2.8 at 03:05Z (small socket/keepalive tweak). We're seeing increased upstream connection reuse which could be exhausting origin. Reverting now to 1.2.7 on a subset.

ops-bot: Rolling revert started for edge pool A. 30% of pool targeted first. Progress: 0/12 pods reverted.

customer-success: Heads up — customers reporting timeouts: PayFlow and Cartly flagged. CS is drafting status update.

sre-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) throttle fanout to origin (disable parallel fanout), 2) increase origin timeout to 12s temporarily, 3) roll back 1.2.8 on pool A, 4) shift small percentage of traffic to region-us-west-2 fallback. Execute in that order.

emma: Throttling fanout now — setting header X-Fanout-Limit:1 via route transform. Command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://config.redwood/api/routes/vhost/payflow" -d '{"transforms": {"set": {"X-Fanout-Limit": "1"}}}'
```
Applied to vhost-payflow and vhost-cartly.

raj: Increasing origin timeout to 12s on LB layer. Pushed. Monitoring p95 origin latency and 504s.

ops-bot: Revert progress: pool A pods reverted 6/12. No errors in rollout so far.

eng-runtime: Revert complete on pool A. Observability: 504 rate dropped to 12% within 90s. Good signal.

emma: Fanout throttle + revert + timeout bump = 504s down to 6% and trending. Rolling out revert to pool B gradually.

alex: Root cause hypothesis: 1.2.8 introduced more aggressive connection reuse which increased head-of-line blocking when origins had transient latency spikes; parallel fanout amplified load. We need postmortem but urgent priority is containment.

customer-success: CS sent status update to affected accounts. No major customer outages, but elevated error rates for high-QPS endpoints.

sre-oncall: Next steps: keep revert until we ship patched proxy with backpressure controls, add circuit-breaker at fanout layer, and run full canary of 1.2.8 with lowered concurrency. Assigning action items: @alex patch + canary plan, @emma update runbooks, @raj validate origin scaling.

alex: Acknowledged. I'll open a PR for connection pool limits + connection health checks and schedule a canary deployment window.

raj: I'll validate origin autoscaling triggers and add temporary increased replicas for payflow origin.

eng-runtime: We'll prepare a patched build 1.2.9 with connection limits and a graceful drain path. ETA 4h.

ops-bot: Monitoring continues. 504s at 2% now. Rolling metrics saved to incident channel. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident Severity: SEV2. Start time: 3869007777. Current status: mitigation in progress, partial rollback complete, customer impact reduced.

sre-oncall: Closing the live triage loop — we'll keep this open for the postmortem. If error rate remains <3% for 30m, we'll demote paging to watch. Thanks all for fast action.
